setup_steps: Same credentials as Blob: storage account access key, connection string, or a container-scoped SAS token.
Enter the filesystem (container) name — ADLS calls buckets filesystems.
For service-principal auth instead of keys: App registrations → client ID + secret, then give it Storage Blob Data Contributor on the account.

airtable.label: Airtable

auth_modes.label: Airtable personal access token
auth_modes.description: API token issued by this service.

setup_steps: Airtable → Builder hub → Personal access tokens → Create token with data.records:read.
Base ID comes from the URL (app…) or the API docs page for your base; Table ID is the tbl… id or table name.
Test proves /v0/{base}/{table} answers — 401/403 is the token or missing scope.

asana.label: Asana

auth_modes.label: Asana personal access token
auth_modes.description: API token issued by this service.

setup_steps: Asana → Apps → Manage developer apps (or developers.asana.com) → Create a Personal Access Token.
Workspace GID: open the workspace in Asana and copy the numeric gid from the URL, or call /workspaces.
The token reads everything the owning user can see — use a service account for least privilege.
Test proves /workspaces answers — 401 is the token, 404 on tasks is a wrong workspace GID.

CSV/TSV: delimiter and header row are detected; set them explicitly if detection guesses wrong.
JSON/JSONL: JSON Lines is one object per line — use it for exports larger than memory.
Parquet/Avro/ORC carry their own schema — mapping is automatic.
Test proves the file opens and parses — a missing path is not Connected.

bigcommerce.label: BigCommerce

auth_modes.label: BigCommerce API account
auth_modes.description: API token issued by this service.

setup_steps: BigCommerce admin → Settings → API accounts → Create API account (V2/V3 token) — grant read on Products, Customers, Orders.
Store hash: the alphanumeric segment in your admin URL — store-abc123.mybigcommerce.com → abc123 (or shown on the API accounts page).
Access token goes in the API key field — it is sent as the X-Auth-Token header.
Test proves v3 products answers — 401 is the token, 404 is a wrong store hash.

bigquery.label: BigQuery

auth_modes.label: Service account JSON
auth_modes.description: JSON key or file path for cloud identity.

fields.label: Service account JSON or file path
fields.hint: Paste the JSON contents from Google Cloud, or enter an absolute path to the key file on the server.

setup_steps: In Google Cloud console → IAM & Admin → Service Accounts, create (or pick) a service account.
Grant it BigQuery Data Viewer on the source dataset, or BigQuery Data Editor + BigQuery Job User on the destination project.
Create a JSON key on the Keys tab and paste the whole JSON into Service account key.
Enter the project ID that owns the datasets — the key carries the identity, the project routes billing/quota.
Test proves the service account can list datasets — PERMISSION_DENIED means the roles, not the key file.

brevo.label: Brevo (Sendinblue)

auth_modes.label: Brevo API key
auth_modes.description: API token issued by this service.

setup_steps: Brevo → SMTP & API → API Keys → Generate a new API key (xkeysib-…).
The key sees contacts, lists, and campaigns for the account — restrict it in Brevo if you want read-only scope.
No domain or tenant field needed — the API key alone identifies the account.
Test proves /contacts answers — 401 is the key.

calendly.label: Calendly

auth_modes.label: Calendly personal access token
auth_modes.description: API token issued by this service.

setup_steps: calendly.com → Integrations → API & webhooks → Generate a personal access token.
User URI: call GET /users/me with the token — the 'uri' field looks like https://api.calendly.com/users/ABCD…
The token sees the owning user's event types and scheduled events only (not the whole org).
Test proves event_types answers — 401 is the token; an empty collection means the User URI is wrong.

setup_steps: Get host and HTTP port (default 8123, or 8443 for TLS). ClickHouse Cloud: service → Connect shows the HTTPS endpoint.
Use the default user or a user with SELECT on source tables / INSERT on the destination database.
Self-hosted: open the port in the firewall — ClickHouse listens on 8123 only on localhost unless configured.
Test proves the HTTP interface answers — a refused connection is the bind/firewall, not auth.

clickup.label: ClickUp

auth_modes.label: ClickUp personal API token
auth_modes.description: API token issued by this service.

setup_steps: ClickUp → Profile → Apps → API Token → copy your pk_ token.
List ID comes from the list's URL or the share link; needed to sync tasks.
Test proves /api/v2/team answers — 401 is the token.

close.label: Close

auth_modes.label: Close API key
auth_modes.description: API token issued by this service.

setup_steps: Close → Settings → API Keys → Generate New API Key.
The key identifies the whole organization — treat it like a password.
Reads cover leads, opportunities and tasks — the API sends the key as the basic-auth username with a blank password.
Test proves /api/v1/lead/ answers — 401 is the key.

confluence.label: Confluence

auth_modes.label: Confluence email + API token
auth_modes.description: API token issued by this service.

setup_steps: id.atlassian.com → Security → API tokens → Create API token.
Site name is your subdomain (acme for acme.atlassian.net); the credential is your account email + API token.
Test proves /wiki/api/v2/spaces answers — 401/403 is the email/token pair.

couchbase.label: Couchbase

auth_modes.label: Username & password
auth_modes.description: Host, username, and password for this system.

setup_steps: Get the cluster host (couchbase://host or host:8091) plus a bucket-scoped user + password.
Capella: cluster → Connect shows the connection string; Database Access holds the credentials.
The user needs Bucket Read on sources or Bucket Write on the destination.
Test proves the cluster manager answers.

dynamodb.label: Amazon DynamoDB

auth_modes.label: AWS access keys
auth_modes.description: Access key ID and secret access key.

fields.label: Custom endpoint URL (optional)
fields.hint: For DynamoDB Local or private AWS-compatible stacks.

setup_steps: Create an IAM access key pair in the AWS console (IAM → Users → Security credentials → Access keys).
Enter Access Key ID, Secret Access Key, and the region your tables live in (e.g. us-east-1).
The IAM policy needs dynamodb:Scan/Query/GetItem on source tables or PutItem/BatchWriteItem on the destination.
Least privilege: scope the policy to the specific table ARNs.
Test proves a list/describe call succeeds — InvalidClientTokenId is a bad key, not a table problem.

elasticsearch.label: Elasticsearch

auth_modes.label: Username & password
auth_modes.description: Host, username, and password for this system.

auth_modes.label: Connection string
auth_modes.description: Login URL. If the password contains @, encode it as %40.

auth_modes.description: API token issued by this service.

fields.label: API key
fields.hint: Enter id:secret for key pairs, or the full encoded key from Elastic Cloud.

setup_steps: Get the endpoint URL (https://host:9200) plus an API key or elastic user + password.
Elastic Cloud: deployment → Manage → copy the endpoint, then Security → API keys to mint a key.
The API key needs read on source indices or create/write on the destination index.
Test proves the cluster answers — 401 is a bad key, a certificate error means TLS/self-signed needs attention.

setup_steps: Get the SMTP host, port (587 starttls or 465 TLS), user, and password/app-password from the mail provider.
Gmail needs an app password (account requires 2-Step Verification first) — the normal password is rejected.
Microsoft 365: smtp.office365.com — ask the admin whether SMTP AUTH is enabled for the mailbox.
Test proves a real authenticated login — 535 is auth, timeout is the port.

auth_modes.label: Freshdesk API key
auth_modes.description: API token issued by this service.

setup_steps: Freshdesk → Profile settings → View API key — the key is the credential (password stays X).
Domain is your helpdesk subdomain — acme in acme.freshdesk.com.
The key inherits the agent's permissions — use an agent that can read tickets/contacts.
Test proves /tickets answers — 401 is the key or domain.

freshservice.label: Freshservice

auth_modes.label: Freshservice API key
auth_modes.description: API token issued by this service.

setup_steps: Freshservice → profile icon → Profile Settings → copy your API key (right sidebar).
Helpdesk domain: the subdomain only — acme for acme.freshservice.com.
The key authenticates as you — it sees every ticket your account can see; use an agent account scoped to the data you want to move.
Test proves /api/v2/tickets answers — 401 is the key, 404 is the domain.

gcs.label: Google Cloud Storage

auth_modes.label: Service account JSON
auth_modes.description: JSON key or file path for cloud identity.

fields.label: Service account JSON or file path
fields.hint: Paste the JSON contents from Google Cloud, or enter an absolute path to the key file on the server.

setup_steps: Console → IAM & Admin → Service Accounts → create a service account.
Grant Storage Object Viewer (read) or Storage Object Admin (write) on the bucket or project.
Keys tab → Add key → JSON — paste the whole JSON into Service account key.
Enter the bucket name exactly as the console shows it.
Test proves bucket listing works — 403 means the role is missing, invalid key JSON means the file was edited.

github.label: GitHub

auth_modes.label: GitHub personal access token
auth_modes.description: Programmatic access token. Snowflake sends it as password=.

setup_steps: GitHub → Settings → Developer settings → Personal access tokens → fine-grained token.
Scope it to the repositories you sync with contents:read and metadata:read.
Enter the token and the owner/repo or organization to read.
Test proves the token answers — 401 is a bad token, 404 means the repo is not in scope.

gitlab.label: GitLab

auth_modes.label: GitLab personal access token
auth_modes.description: API token issued by this service.

setup_steps: GitLab → User Settings → Personal access tokens → create one with read_api scope.
Self-managed GitLab: enter your instance URL (https://gitlab.your-company.com/api/v4); gitlab.com works by default.
The token reads projects, issues, and merge requests across the groups it can see — use a bot/service account for full visibility.
Test proves /projects answers — 401 is the token, 404 is the base URL.

fields.label: API token

setup_steps: Settings → Integrations → Private Apps → create a private app.
Give it the scopes the sync needs: crm.objects.contacts.read (and .write for destinations), plus companies/deals as required.
Copy the access token it shows — paste it in the token field.
Test proves the token answers — 401 is a revoked or mistyped token, 403 is a missing scope.

iceberg.label: Apache Iceberg

auth_modes.label: Warehouse path
auth_modes.description: Local or mounted lakehouse root. No REST/Glue committer.

fields.label: Warehouse root
fields.hint: Filesystem CoW writer. Overwrite leftover MERGE lists dest-engine file footers. Incremental leftover MERGE is a hard no-op.

fields.label: Default namespace (optional)
fields.hint: Used as the Iceberg namespace folder under the warehouse when set. Table name is chosen in Transfer Studio.

auth_modes.label: REST catalog
auth_modes.description: REST catalog URI plus warehouse. Overwrite leftover MERGE is dest-engine catalog snapshot + delete.

fields.label: REST catalog URI
fields.hint: Iceberg REST catalog. Leftover MERGE commits deletes through RestCatalog. Glue and Nessie stay Planned.

fields.label: Warehouse
fields.hint: Object-store or file warehouse the REST catalog commits into.

setup_steps: Iceberg tables live in a catalog — pick the one your platform issues credentials for: AWS Glue, a REST catalog, or Hadoop (warehouse path).
Glue: IAM access keys with glue:GetTable/GetDatabase plus S3 read/write on the warehouse location.
REST catalog (e.g. Polaris, Nessie, Tabular): catalog URI + bearer token or client credentials.
Enter the warehouse location (s3://bucket/warehouse/) and the namespace the tables live in.
Test proves the catalog lists namespaces — a 404 is the URI, a 403 is IAM.

jira.label: Jira Cloud

auth_modes.description: API token issued by this service.

The account needs Browse projects permission on the projects you read.
Test proves /rest/api/3/myself answers — 401 is email/token, not the site URL.

The principal needs Read/Describe on source topics or Write/Create on destination topics.

klaviyo.label: Klaviyo

auth_modes.label: Klaviyo private API key
auth_modes.description: API token issued by this service.

setup_steps: Klaviyo → Settings → API keys → Create Private API Key with read access to the objects you sync.
Private keys start with pk_ — public site keys cannot read the API.
The revision header is pinned to 2024-10-15; no extra config needed.
Test proves /lists answers — 401 is the private key.

auth_modes.label: Mailchimp API key
auth_modes.description: API token issued by this service.

fields.label: Data center

setup_steps: Mailchimp → Account → Extras → API keys → Create A Key.
The data center is the key's suffix (key-us21 → dc us21) — it is derived automatically if you only paste the key.
Any username works for Mailchimp basic auth — the key is the credential.
Test proves /lists answers — 401 is the key, not the data center.

mailjet.label: Mailjet

Both are required — the API key is the username, the Secret key is the password.
Test proves /v3/REST/contact answers — 401 is the key pair.

Self-hosted: use mongodb://host:27017/database and the user's credentials.
The user needs read on the source databases (find/listCollections) or readWrite on the destination.
Atlas also needs your server's egress IP in Network Access — a timeout usually means the IP is not whitelisted, not bad credentials.
CDC and snapshot-consistent reads need a replica set — standalone mongod cannot do them.

auth_modes.description: Login URL. If the password contains @, encode it as %40.

fields.label: Connection string
fields.hint: SQLAlchemy-style login URL. If the password contains @, encode it as %40 — or use Username & password.

setup_steps: Get host, port (default 3306), database, user, and password from your DBA or console (RDS → Connectivity, Cloud SQL, PlanetScale → Connect, Aiven → Service).
MariaDB, Percona, PlanetScale, SingleStore, and Aurora MySQL share this driver — same fields.
Grant the user SELECT on source tables or INSERT/CREATE on the destination schema.
Or paste a connection string: mysql://user:pass@host:3306/db.
For CDC or incremental syncs the user also needs REPLICATION privileges on MySQL.
Test proves TCP reachability plus login — Access denied means the password or host grant (user@host) is wrong.

neo4j.label: Neo4j

auth_modes.label: Username & password
auth_modes.description: Host, username, and password for this system.

setup_steps: Get the Bolt endpoint (host:7687) — Aura shows it under Connection URI.
Use the neo4j user or a user with read access on the source database.
Aura requires TLS — keep encryption on.
Test proves the Bolt handshake answers — unauthorized is credentials, timeout is routing.

notion.label: Notion

auth_modes.label: Notion integration token
auth_modes.description: API token issued by this service.

setup_steps: notion.so/my-integrations → New integration → copy the Internal Integration Secret (secret_…).
Critical: Notion only returns what the integration can see — open each page/database → ••• → Connections → add your integration, or reads come back empty.
Database rows need the Database ID — the 32-char hex in the database URL.
Test proves POST /search answers — 401 is the token; an empty result means the workspace hasn't shared the object.

auth_modes.label: Username & password
auth_modes.description: Host, username, and password for this system.

setup_steps: Get host, port (default 1521), service name (or SID), user, and password from your DBA — the service name is usually in tnsnames.ora.
Autonomous Database: download the wallet and use the full connect descriptor or service name it defines.
The user needs SELECT on the source tables (or the destination schema privileges).
Test proves the listener answers and the login works — ORA-01017 is bad credentials, ORA-12541 is host/port.
